evals.prompt: Our Python AWS Lambda function in a VPC times out intermittently on reader queries to **ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey** and crashes at import time during unit tests when the cache is unreachable. Audit our security groups, IAM auth token lifetime, and `valkey-py` connection lifecycle.
evals.expected_output: Reads `references/shared-runtime/lambda.md` and `references/shared-security/vpc-patterns.md` to diagnose all three issues: (1) **ElastiCache Serverless uses port `6379` (primary) AND port `6380` (reader endpoint)** — security groups allowing only `6379` drop `6380` reader connections causing timeouts; (2) **never initialize `valkey-py` at module import time** — lazily initialize and cache the client inside a helper function called at invocation time so unit tests don't crash on import; and (3) generate short-lived `elasticache:connect` SigV4 IAM auth tokens (`<= 900s` / 15-minute expiry) refreshed before expiration with TLS always enabled on Serverless.
expectations: Activates the amazon-elasticache skill
Identifies the missing port `6380` reader-endpoint rule alongside port `6379` in the Serverless VPC Security Group
Fixes import-time crashes via lazy function-scoped `valkey-py` client initialization and configures TLS + `<= 15 min` (`900s`) IAM auth token refresh

evals.prompt: After enabling cluster mode on our 6-shard Valkey cluster, `MGET` and `MULTI/EXEC` pipelines fail with `CROSSSLOT Keys in request don't hash to the same slot`, and after adding `{global}` hash tags to every key, Shard 1 hit `98%` CPU while Shards 2–6 sit at `4%`. Diagnose both issues and fix the key schema.
evals.expected_output: Consults `references/shared-ux/error-remediation.md` and `references/monitoring/`: (1) explains `CROSSSLOT` occurs in cluster mode (`16,384` hash slots) when multi-key operations (`MGET`, `MULTI/EXEC`, Lua scripts) touch keys hashing to different slots (and notes `MULTI/EXEC` + IAM auth / cluster caveats); (2) explains wrapping every key in a static `{global}` hash tag forces **100% of keys onto a single hash slot on Shard 1**, causing severe slot/memory/CPU skew; and (3) fixes it by scoping hash tags to high-cardinality entity boundaries (`user:{userId}:profile`, `user:{userId}:cart`), splitting cross-entity `MGET` into per-slot/pipelined requests, and using Valkey 8.0/8.1 per-slot metrics & `COMMANDLOG` / read replicas or L1 local caching for genuine hot keys.
expectations: Activates the amazon-elasticache skill
Explains `CROSSSLOT` across the 16,384 hash slots and why `{global}` pinned every key onto a single slot/shard
Prescribes high-cardinality entity hash tags (`{userId}`/`{tenantId}`), pipelined/slot-grouped multi-key fetches, and Valkey per-slot/hot-key diagnostics
